findings.issue_category: public bucket ACL / no public access block
findings.description: The 'data' bucket is created with no public access block and is annotated as public (no private ACL set, comments confirm intent), allowing anonymous read/write of objects such as the customer master file uploaded into it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so sensitive customer data stored in this bucket is not encrypted with SSE-KMS.
The bucket has no logging block, so unauthorized access to the sensitive objects it holds cannot be detected or investigated.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects deleted or overwritten by an attacker (combined with force_destroy = true) cannot be recovered.

A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded to the unencrypted, publicly accessible 'data' bucket and no server-side encryption (kms_key_id / server_side_encryption) is specified on the object, exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial data stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to financial data is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose financial data publicly without any account-level guardrail.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so accidental or malicious deletion of financial objects is unrecoverable.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the operations bucket, so its contents are stored unencrypted.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit trail of object access for this bucket.
No public access block is attached, so there is no guardrail preventing a future ACL or policy change from making the bucket public.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so datasets are stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, leaving it without account-level protection against accidental public exposure.
The central log bucket has no public access block resource; because log data can reveal internal infrastructure detail, an accidental policy change exposing it would be high impact.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The log bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or exfiltration of audit logs would go unrecorded.
No bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport is attached to any bucket in this file, so objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
